body:
Slice 3 of 6 of #635. Depends on #649.

## What

- GC's reference build resolves segmented maps by bounded `seg:` ranges; `ReferenceSet` gains `unresolvable`; scrub (which calls the reference build) inherits it;
- per-object fail-closed containment: an undecodable/unresolvable object never aborts the pass, is never reclaimed, and blocks certification — `reconciliation.rs` reports `Reconciled::Blocked`;
- fixes the finding still open at #647's close: with one unresolvable object, `protects()` short-circuits `true`, so GC audits every otherwise-unprotected fleet fragment as `skip reason="referenced"` and still returns `Satisfied` (gc.rs:163-214 in the closed PR) — while scrub returns `Blocked` for the identical condition. GC must report `Blocked` exactly as scrub does; a partial reference set never certifies.

## Scope

`crates/custodian/src/{gc,scrub,reconciliation}.rs`, their tests, and the shared `segmented_map_consumers.rs` fixture (its GC/scrub legs).

## Out of scope

restore / reconstruction / backfill / rebalance (slice 4).

## Acceptance

- a segmented object's fragments survive GC + scrub, and a drain of a server holding them answers `Pending` (the positive observable — "GC deleted nothing" passes vacuously);
- with one unresolvable inode, GC and scrub both return `Blocked`, never `Satisfied`, and reclaim nothing of that object;
- `cargo xtask ci` green.

Part of #635 / #508 / epic #513.
